profiles.meeting_scenario: A planning meeting in a hospital radiation oncology department to organize a retrospective dosimetric comparison study of low-dose-rate prostate brachytherapy planning approaches. The team is preparing an internal study package for abstract submission and needs to decide how they will extract contours and dosimetric endpoints from existing TRUS and MRI data for 26 prior implant cases, how the three retrospective planning techniques will be reconstructed, who will handle each step, and when the analysis set will be ready. The agenda is to align on the cohort pull, what counts as the 'delivered plan' comparator, how to build the retrospective 4D Brachytherapy and MRI loose-seed plans, what dosimetric summary tables to produce, and the timeline for plan generation and statistics. The expected outcome is a concrete work plan assigning contour review, retrospective replanning, endpoint extraction, and statistical comparison tasks over the next three weeks.

members.name: Dr. Priya Raman
members.role: Radiation Oncologist and Brachytherapy Study Lead
members.expertise: LDR prostate brachytherapy, intraoperative TRUS workflow, clinical dosimetry interpretation
members.background: Attending physician who has led the department's prostate brachytherapy program for six years and routinely reviews implant quality using post-implant and intraoperative dosimetry.
members.private_state: Wants the project to move quickly into abstract form using a clinically familiar framing and is trying to minimize rework by relying on conventions from prior implant QA reviews.
hidden_assumptions: When the team says 'delivered plan,' it naturally means the final intraoperative plan that was actually used to implant the patient after any live adjustments in the operating room.

If they agree to use 'MRI measurements,' everyone will use the same clinical prostate contour already described in the radiology-linked planning workflow rather than redefining apex/base boundaries from scratch.

A 'complete dosimetry table' for this kind of comparison means one final patient-level endpoint set per technique, suitable for paired statistical testing, not intermediate slice-by-slice or draft exports.
Having the data 'ready by Friday' means ready for her to review in the shared departmental drive by close of business local time.

members.name: Alex Chen
members.expertise: Brachytherapy treatment planning systems, retrospective replanning, image registration, dose-metric extraction
members.background: Physicist responsible for QA of prostate implant planning software and for generating retrospective comparison plans for departmental research projects.
members.private_state: Wants the analysis to be technically reproducible and comparable across modalities, and is trying to avoid using clinically edited artifacts that could introduce undocumented bias.
hidden_assumptions: When people refer to the 'delivered plan' in a retrospective methods section, they usually mean the archived pre-implant approved plan in the planning system because that is the stable, reproducible object available for extraction.

Using 'MRI measurements' implies recontouring the prostate directly on MRI according to a consistent retrospective research rule set, even if that differs slightly from the clinical contour used at the time.
A 'complete dosimetry table' includes both the endpoint spreadsheet and the exported plan/structure references needed to reproduce how each value was generated.
If the study needs to be 'ready by Friday,' it is acceptable to upload by the end of the day after his automated extraction finishes overnight, effectively Friday-night completion.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as the delivered plan
misalignment_points.surface_form: They repeatedly agree to compare each retrospective technique against 'the delivered plan.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means the final intraoperative loose-seed TRUS plan reflecting any seed-count or placement adjustments made during the implant procedure.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means the archived approved plan saved before the case began, because it is the fixed planning object easiest to retrieve consistently for all 26 patients.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In brachytherapy meetings, 'delivered plan' is a familiar shorthand and both versions exist inside the same patient's chart; because both are plausibly connected to what was delivered clinically, the phrase feels specific enough and neither expects ambiguity.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the 4D Brachytherapy arm will use 'MRI measurements' and that MRI can be integrated into the workflow.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 means using the prostate dimensions derived from the clinically available MRI contouring approach already used in prior multidisciplinary review, including conventional handling of base and apex based on the diagnostic report context.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 means freshly deriving dimensions from a standardized retrospective MRI contour he will create directly in the planning software using his own reproducibility rules.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both are talking about measurements from the same MRI study and the downstream use is the same webBXT nomogram, so 'MRI measurements' sounds operationally settled even though the source contouring convention differs.

misalignment_points.topic: What it means to have the dosimetry table complete
misalignment_points.surface_form: They align on producing a 'complete dosimetry table' for all 26 cases before statistics.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 believes complete means one cleaned final spreadsheet with the agreed endpoints per patient and per technique: prostate V100, V150, D90, rectum D0.1cc, D2cc, urethra D10, and D30, ready for statistical testing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 believes complete means the spreadsheet plus linked export files, plan identifiers, and contour provenance notes so the table can be audited and reproduced before any statistical handoff.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both share the same phrase and both think they are being thorough; the additional reproducibility package M2 assumes is standard research hygiene, while M1 treats it as background documentation rather than part of the completion criterion.

misalignment_points.surface_form: They agree that the first analysis set will be 'ready by Friday.'
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: M1 presupposes Friday means accessible for her daytime review before she leaves clinic on Friday afternoon.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: M2 presupposes Friday means he can finish the batch runs and upload the materials later that evening after machine time opens up.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Deadline language like 'by Friday' is routine and usually left unqualified in internal planning; because neither is resisting the deadline, the phrase signals agreement rather than a need to negotiate specifics.

If we keep the framing close to our usual implant QA language, I can draft the abstract efficiently and avoid rework later.

I'll pull the TRUS and MRI studies, rebuild each retrospective technique in a consistent way, and generate a complete dosimetry table that includes not just the endpoint values but also the plan references and contour provenance so nothing is opaque later.
